applicability.rule: A process is tagged to one commodity ONLY where it acts on an asset class, hazard or regulatory regime that exists in that commodity alone. Everything else is tagged to both. Group and category labels are derived from the process tags, never assigned directly.

labels.common: every process applies to both commodities
labels.mixed: a blend - the group appears in both views but with different content

views.Combined: all processes - for a dual-commodity utility
views.Gas: processes where gas is in applies
views.Electric: processes where electric is in applies

meta.scope_note: Front of meter only. This reference covers the regulated utility: moving gas or electricity across a network it owns, under a regulatory regime, up to the meter. Behind-the-meter home services - selling, installing and servicing customer-owned heating, cooling, water heating, generation, electrical and plumbing equipment - is a different business with its own process model, held separately in '02 Industry Specialization/Behind the Meter Home Services'. The two commonly share a call centre and a work management platform; that is shared tooling, not a shared process model.
meta.revision_note: Revised 2026-08-26 by three-platform Round 1 consensus (ChatGPT, Grok, Claude): added distribution integrity programme (9.8), public awareness (9.9) and wildfire operational response (10.6); operator qualification (14.2.5-6); DER interconnection (11.6.6-7); valve, vault, structure and electrical-diagnostic inspection (9.1.5-8); abandonment (9.6.6); avian protection (9.5.5); damage-assessment refresh (10.2.5); mutual-aid demobilisation (10.4.6); management of change (12.6.4); ISO 14224-aligned failure wording (4.3.6, 12.4.2); pressure testing retagged gas-only (9.1.3). See _Collab/30_consensus/CONSENSUS_ROUND1_Change_Log.md. Round 2 (2026-08-26): consensus ratified 14-0 on the resolved divergences; 9.8.7 annual integrity reporting split from 9.8.5; 'written' restored on 9.8.1/9.9.1; 10.6.1 narrowed to operational response; 4.4.5 SCADA point-to-point verification added as the work-side control-room hook; ISO 55001:2024 and GFMAM v3.0 mapping merged into meta.standards_mapping.
meta.failure_coding_note: Failure recording (4.3.6 capture, 12.4.2 validate) is anchored to ISO 14224 data structures - equipment class, failure mode, mechanism, cause, impact - with a documented electric-distribution equivalent where ISO 14224 classes do not fit.
meta.standards_mapping_note: Mapped by Round 2 three-platform consensus (see meta.standards_mapping). The reference maps operating content to ISO 55001:2024 clause families and GFMAM Landscape v3.0 subjects; it does not claim conformity or alignment, and the management-system shell is deliberately out of scope.
meta.decisions_2026_08_26: Tim, 2026-08-26: (1) WT7 Reimbursable / Third-Party Work added so the work-type classification stays mutually exclusive - joint-use make-ready, customer-contribution construction and damage-claim repairs are neither the utility's capital nor its O&M. (2) Retail service plans, contracts and lead generation belong in the Home Services reference, not this model - the mixed regulated/retail view was a carryover from a prior client that ran both businesses in one company. The regime axis stays retired here. (3) Control-room operations: EXCLUDED from this reference - continuous network operation, not discrete work; obligations land in SCADA/DMS platforms, not the EAM/field systems this reference scopes. Knowledge preserved in the Control Room Operations Companion deck and research/Control Room - Research Note.md, including the proposed group 10.5 verbatim and the criteria for reopening.
meta.scope_exclusions: Deliberately out of scope: real-time network and control-room operations (gas control under 49 CFR 192.631; the electric distribution operations centre), SCADA/DMS operation, fleet garage maintenance, and LNG facilities (49 CFR 193). The model covers the work-management interfaces to these (4.4.4, 10.3.2, 10.1, 9.6.3), not the operations themselves.

standards_mapping.method: Round 2 three-platform consensus, 2026-08-26. A clause or subject maps where at least two of three independent mappings placed it; primary where at least two placed it primary. This maps operating content only - it asserts no conformity with ISO 55001:2024 and no coverage of the GFMAM Landscape; the management-system shell (leadership, policy, SAMP, audit, management review) is deliberately out of scope. Verify subject wording against the purchased texts before client use.
standards_mapping.iso55001_2024_notes: Official 4.5 title is 'Asset management decision-making' (value is its purpose, not its name). 7.6 Data and information is revised and retitled, not new; 7.7 Knowledge is new; 8.3 is the 2024 renaming of outsourcing; 10.3 predictive action replaces preventive action.
standards_mapping.gfmam_v3_notes: Third Edition, June 2024: 7 groups, 40 subjects. Data and Information subjects carry the full 'Asset Management Data and Information ...' names.

layers.Work Lifecycle: 1.0-5.0. Runs in sequence for a single piece of work.
layers.Specialised Operations: 6.0-11.0. Each runs the full lifecycle inside its own operational discipline.
layers.Foundations and Enabling: 12.0-16.0. Supplies assets, materials, workforce, information and external delivery capacity to every lifecycle stage rather than sitting inside the sequence.
layers.Asset Lifecycle: 17.0-19.0. The asset's own life - planned, created, operated and retired - as distinct from the work performed on it. Appended 2026-08-29 without renumbering anything: categories 1.0 to 16.0 keep their ids, uids and legacy_ids.

sourcing.principle: Contracting is a delivery mode, not a lifecycle stage. Categories 1.0 to 5.0 run once for a piece of work whoever performs it; 16.0 holds the processes that exist only because the performer is external - qualification, award, oversight, settlement and system federation - and attaches to the lifecycle at named points rather than sitting between two of its stages.
sourcing.why_not_a_stage: No process framework consulted places supplier or contractor management as a sequential step inside a work lifecycle. ISO 55001:2024 puts the whole asset lifecycle in clause 8.1 and external provision beside it in 8.3. ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.1 requires that outsourced processes be controlled and points at 8.4, whose Annex A.8 covers purchasing, associate-company arrangements and process outsourcing in one clause. GFMAM Landscape v3.0 calls 6.2 Asset Creation and Acquisition a stage in the asset life cycle and describes 6.8 Supply Chain Management as operating over the entire life cycle. APQC states that its numbering does not imply order, and inserts no supplier stage into any of its own execute-then-close sequences. TM Forum eTOM models Supplier/Partner Relationship Management as a horizontal grouping supporting Fulfillment, Assurance and Billing. ASCM SCOR v14 moved contracts and agreements out of Source into the cross-cutting Orchestrate layer.
sourcing.hook_note: Group-level hooks are recorded on each 16.x group. They are attachment points, not a sequence: 16.1 runs before any specific work exists, 16.3 runs concurrently with 4.0, and 16.4 straddles 5.0.

meta.stable_ids: Every category, group and process carries uid, a permanent element id that never changes and is never reused. The dotted id is positional and may change when the framework is restructured - it is an index, not an identity. This follows APQC practice, where element id 10280 'Manage suppliers' keeps its identity while its dotted number differs between the cross-industry and utilities frameworks. Pre-2026-08-28 numbering is recorded as legacy_id and in build/eam/id_crosswalk.csv.
meta.renumbering_note: Renumbered 2026-08-28 by the structural revision. Dotted ids quoted in revision_note and in the Round 1 and Round 2 change logs are the pre-revision numbering and are deliberately left as written, because those are dated records. Use build/eam/id_crosswalk.csv to translate.
meta.structural_revision_note: Revised 2026-08-28. Manage Contractors and Partners moved from 5.0 in the work lifecycle to 16.0 in Foundations and Enabling; Close Work, Settle Cost and Update Records moved 6.0 to 5.0; the specialised block became contiguous at 6.0-11.0 and Joint Use moved 16.0 to 11.0, ending the one category that sat outside its own band. Content, counts and commodity tags are unchanged - this is a placement and numbering change only. See _Collab/30_consensus/STRUCTURAL_REVISION_Change_Log.md.

lifecycle_axis._why: The model is organised on a WORK axis - identify, plan, schedule, execute, close. APQC and GFMAM are organised on an ASSET axis - plan and acquire, design and construct, operate, maintain, dispose. The work axis is what happens inside 'maintain'. Both are valid; carrying both lets the model answer ISO 55001:2024 cl. 8.1 without abandoning the granularity that makes it a process model rather than a benchmarking taxonomy.
lifecycle_axis._all: 'all' marks an enabling category that serves every stage rather than sitting at one of them.

meta.asset_lifecycle_note: Categories 17.0 to 19.0 close six themes that APQC PCF Utilities and the GFMAM Asset Management Landscape independently found absent: planned outage and switching, asset operation, asset creation and commissioning, network demand analysis, capital programme and whole-life value, and decommissioning and disposal. Two independent organisations plus ISO 55001:2024 cl. 8.1 meets this repository's promotion rule. See research/The Asset Lifecycle Gap - Finding.md. 18.0 is scoped work-facing only by decision: real-time monitoring, alarms, optimisation and protection settings are SCADA, ADMS and DERMS functions.
